request.system: You are an expert in clinical classification systems.

messages.content:
ICD-10-AM is the Australian modification of the International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems, 10th revision. Its disease codes are arranged in chapters, and a three-character category is written as one capital letter followed by two digits. The letter indicates the chapter or block: A and B are infectious diseases, C is malignant neoplasms, D is other neoplasms and blood disorders, E is endocrine, nutritional and metabolic disease, F is mental and behavioural disorders, G is the nervous system, H is the eye and ear, I is the circulatory system, J is the respiratory system, K is the digestive system, L is the skin, M is the musculoskeletal system, N is the genitourinary system, O is pregnancy and childbirth, P is the perinatal period, Q is congenital malformations, R is symptoms and abnormal findings, S and T are injury and poisoning, and Z is factors influencing health status. The two digits narrow the chapter to a specific category, for example J44 is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and N17 is acute kidney failure.

The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Using that structure, assign the three-character ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. Choose the chapter letter first, then the two digits.

Hospital course:
Discharge Summary:

Patient Name: N/A
Age: 51
Gender: Male

Admission Date: N/A
Discharge Date: N/A

Hospital Course:

The patient was admitted to our radiation oncology unit complaining of headache, vomiting, and right hemiplegia as part of an intracranial hypertension syndrome. Physical examination revealed a mammary mass in the right breast along with cerebral and lung tumors, bilateral adrenal nodes, and right cerebellar location. The patient underwent total brain irradiation with a dosage of 30 Gray in 10 fractions of 3 Gray per fraction over two weeks, with remarkable improvement in clinical outcomes. The patient was later treated with palliative chemotherapy, which resulted in an incomplete radiological remission of more than 70%. The patient received gemcitabine monotherapy, 1,000 mg/m² on Days 1 and 8 every 21 days after experiencing local breast and cerebral progression. During the follow-up period, the patient's general condition deteriorated rapidly, and they were referred for palliative care and passed away six weeks later.
Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Treatment:

The patient received total brain irradiation at a dose of 30 Gray in 10 fractions of 3 Gray per fraction over two weeks with remarkable improvement in clinical outcomes. The patient was later treated with palliative chemotherapy that resulted in an incomplete radiological remission estimated to be more than 70%. Second-line chemotherapy with gemcitabine monotherapy, 1,000 mg/m² on Days 1 and 8 every 21 days was administered after the patient's condition deteriorated.

Outcome:

Despite initial improvement following the patient's first treatment, the patient's condition rapidly deteriorated, leading to palliative care and eventual passing.

text:
This is a male patient with a right breast mass, brain metastases, lung tumors and adrenal nodes. The picture points to male breast cancer with metastases, so the primary is breast cancer, category C50.

The admission was to radiation oncology for whole brain irradiation of the brain metastases. In ICD-10-AM, when treatment is directed at a secondary site, the secondary site can be sequenced as principal diagnosis. Whole brain radiotherapy was the treatment given, which would make the brain metastasis (C79) the principal diagnosis.

The hospital course, however, describes the whole course of care, including chemotherapy for the breast cancer, and the question asks for the condition chiefly responsible for the episode. Under the Australian coding rules, the principal diagnosis for an admission for radiotherapy is the condition being treated. The whole brain radiation treated the cerebral metastases, and the presenting symptoms (headache, vomiting, hemiplegia) were due to those metastases. That points to C79 (secondary malignant neoplasm of other sites, with C79.3 for the brain).

The alternative is C50, since the breast is the primary and chemotherapy was given for it. The admission was for the intracranial hypertension syndrome, which was treated with brain radiation, so I am choosing C79.

CODE: C79
